title: Strategic Competition and Convergence in LLM Leaderboards
abstract: arXiv:2611.09780v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Leaderboards are a popular way to compare large language model (LLM) capabilities and can influence how model developers invest resources. We ask when competition on leaderboards leads developers to produce models with similar capability profiles, which we call monoculture, or similar performance levels. We study this by formulating leaderboard competition as a game in which model developers invest resources across capabilities to maximize their win rate. We show that similar production functions can induce similar capability profiles, while comparative advantage can sustain distinct capability profiles. We then study convergence in performance levels and show that diminishing returns can lead to an increasingly crowded competitive frontier. translated_title: LLM排行榜中的策略性竞争与收敛
translated_abstract: 排行榜是比较大语言模型（LLM）能力的流行方式，并且能够影响模型开发者如何投入资源。我们探讨排行榜上的竞争何时会导致开发者生产出具有相似能力画像（我们称之为“单一文化”）的模型，或达到相似的性能水平。为此，我们将排行榜竞争形式化为一个博弈，其中模型开发者在各项能力上投入资源以最大化其胜率。我们证明，相似的生产函数可以诱导出相似的能力画像，而比较优势则可以维持不同的能力画像。随后我们研究性能水平的收敛性，并证明收益递减会导致竞争前沿日益拥挤。利用来自LM Arena和OpenRouter的数据，我们发现开发者在落后于竞争对手的类别上改进更多，同时仍保留特定类别的优势。与此同时，我们发现……
tldr: 该论文将LLM排行榜竞争建模为开发者跨能力分配资源的博弈，揭示了相似的生产函数会导致模型能力趋同（单一文化），而比较优势可维持差异化，并以LM Arena和OpenRouter的数据验证了开发者会在落后领域加速追赶但仍保留类别特有优势。
en_tdlr: By modeling LLM leaderboard competition as a game where developers allocate resources across capabilities, this paper shows that similar production functions drive capability convergence ("monoculture") while comparative advantage sustains distinct profiles, with empirical evidence that developers improve faster in lagging categories yet retain category-specific advantages.
